title: Heat wave risk, alerts and worker protections in Singapore
asked: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye asked what risk Singapore faces from heat waves like those in Malaysia and Thailand, and whether advance warning systems for weather-dependent sectors will be enhanced.
response: Dr Janil Puthucheary said a heat wave is declared when the daily maximum temperature averaged across all weather stations is at least 35oC for three consecutive days and the average daily mean temperature throughout the period is at least 29oC. He said the chance of a heat wave in Singapore for the rest of the 2026 hot season, ending in May, is low. MSS issues fortnightly outlooks and four-day forecasts, monitors El Niño and works with the Mercury Taskforce to issue advisories, including to weather-dependent sectors. Heat stress management runs regardless of a heat wave forecast, including the Heat Stress Advisory and MOM's heat stress framework for outdoor work.

key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS) issues fortnightly outlooks and four-day forecasts of weather conditions, including high temperatures.

key_points.point: MSS monitors climate phenomena such as El Niño and works with the Mercury Taskforce to issue advisories, including to weather-dependent sectors, if extended high temperatures are expected.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: MSS also closely monitors climate phenomena, such as El Niño, and works with the Mercury Taskforce to issue advisories, including to weather-dependent sectors, if it expects extended periods of high temperatures.

key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary

key_points.point: The Heat Resilience Policy Office announced in the Committee of Supply this year will coordinate across the whole-of-Government on these issues.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: these issues are the sorts of things that the Heat Resilience Policy Office that we announced in the Committee of Supply this year will indeed coordinate across the whole-of-Government

key_points.point: The Heat Resilience Policy Office will take up work on the urban heat island effect and worker protections.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: this is work that the Heat Resilience Policy Office will indeed be taking up.

left_open: Whether existing heat stress guidelines for employers remain adequate under more prolonged or intense heat.
Whether formal protections or guidance will be extended to indoor, non-air-conditioned workplaces and delivery riders.
How the urban heat island effect may amplify heat stress and how it is factored into national heat resilience planning.
Whether the number of sensors will be increased.
Whether a more formalised alert system with clear thresholds and corresponding response measures will be introduced.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered the robustness of heat alerts, sensor coverage, urban heat island effects and worker protections.
